name: Amariah
overview: Amariah was a male Levite, specifically identified as a descendant of Hebron, who belonged to the Hebronite family originating from Kohath, son of Levi. This lineage situates him within the priestly tribe of Levi, emphasizing his role in the religious heritage of Israel. His heritage is noted in 1 Chronicles 23:19, linking him to a significant Levitical family line.
namesAndTitles: The name Amariah means 'YHWH has said,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord's authority and declaration. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:19, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaning that highlights divine communication.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Amariah as a descendant of Hebron, placing him within the Hebronite branch of the Levites. No additional family relationships beyond this lineage are provided in the biblical text referenced.
scriptureSignificance: Amariah's significance lies in his identification as part of the Levitical priestly line descending from Hebron, which underscores the organization and heritage of the priestly families serving in Israel. His mention in 1 Chronicles 23:19 situates him within the broader context of Levitical duties and the preservation of the covenantal worship established by God. This connection highlights the continuity of God's appointed priesthood through generations.
